answer: Agents can require every participant to post a refundable stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated identities or collusive trades. A single operator may mint a thousand accounts, but each must lock scarce capital, and suspicious clusters risk losing it; honest agents recover their stake after review. The saffron market can use a lantern-lit audit queue to flag accounts sharing payment sources, while a pearl-sized deposit still makes mass identities costly rather than free.
